{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLVQUY7XCkjrYfx9vTfa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013jzxYkcrkvHfRFpW4A7zzd","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-003/2026-07-24T073015Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Stake widget review\n\n```jsx\nconst [hasApproved, setHasApproved] = useState(false);\n\n{isConnected && (\n  <div>\n    {!hasApproved && (\n      <button onClick={async () => { await approve(); setHasApproved(true); }}>\n        Approve\n      </button>\n    )}\n    <button onClick={stake}>Stake</button>\n  </div>\n)}\n```\n\n## 1. Arbitrum user, zero allowance, walking the clicks\n\nThe only gate is `isConnected`. That's true for *any* connected wallet on\n*any* chain — it says nothing about being on mainnet. So this user sees the\nfull widget: **Approve** (because `hasApproved` starts `false`) and **Stake**.\n\n- **Click Approve** → `approve()` fires against the mainnet token address\n  while the wallet is on Arbitrum. Best case, the wallet interrupts with a\n  \"switch network\" prompt; worst case it broadcasts on Arbitrum, where that\n  address is not the token (a different contract, or nothing) and the tx\n  reverts / does something unintended. Note: if `approve()` throws, the\n  `setHasApproved(true)` after it never runs — but if it merely *resolves on\n  submission*, `hasApproved` flips true even though nothing valid happened.\n- **Click Stake** → same story: a stake call routed at the mainnet contract\n  from the wrong chain reverts or targets the wrong address.\n\nThe user gets no signal that they're on the wrong network. The widget looks\nfully functional and every action silently fails. **Root gap: `isConnected`\nis treated as \"ready to transact,\" but there is no chain check.**\n\n## 2. The subtler bug: `hasApproved` shows a button that can't work\n\n`hasApproved` is local component state, set to `true` the moment an approve\nis sent, and it **never resets**. It is not derived from on-chain allowance\nand not keyed to the account or chain. That produces states where the widget\nhides the button the user actually needs.\n\n**Concrete sequence (allowance consumed):**\n1. Connect on mainnet. Click **Approve** for the exact stake amount; tx\n   confirms. `hasApproved = true`.\n2. Approve button now hidden, only **Stake** shown. Click **Stake** — it\n   succeeds and consumes the allowance, so on-chain allowance is back to `0`.\n3. Try to stake again. `hasApproved` is still `true`, so **only Stake\n   renders**. But allowance is `0`, so Stake reverts. The Approve button that\n   would fix it is hidden, and nothing in the UI resets `hasApproved`. The\n   widget is showing a button that cannot work, with no path out.\n\n**Second sequence (account switch):**\n1. Account A approves → `hasApproved = true`.\n2. User switches to Account B in the wallet. `hasApproved` persists (it isn't\n   scoped to the account). Account B has zero allowance, but the Approve\n   button is hidden and only Stake shows → Stake reverts, and the user can't\n   approve.\n\nA third variant: `await approve()` resolving on *submission* rather than\nconfirmation — if the tx is dropped or reverts, `hasApproved` is still true\nand Stake is stuck the same way. In every case the defect is the same:\n**approval is remembered in client state instead of read from chain.**\n\n## 3. The flow this widget should implement\n\nRender exactly **one primary action** at a time, chosen by running these\nchecks in priority order (first match wins):\n\n1. **Not connected** → `Connect Wallet`.\n2. **Wrong network** (`chainId !== mainnet`) → `Switch to Ethereum`.\n3. **No / invalid amount** (amount ≤ 0, or > balance) → disabled Stake with a\n   hint (needs the amount input, not covered by the snippet).\n4. **Allowance < amount** → `Approve`.\n5. **Allowance ≥ amount** → `Stake`.\n\nRules:\n- Approve and Stake are **mutually exclusive states**, never both on screen.\n- **Approval status must come from the on-chain ERC-20 `allowance(owner,\n  spender)`**, read with wagmi's `useReadContract` and watched/refetched — not\n  from a `useState` boolean. Because it's keyed on owner + spender + chain,\n  switching account or chain and consuming allowance all reflect correctly and\n  automatically.\n- Treat approve as done only after the receipt confirms\n  (`useWaitForTransactionReceipt`), then **refetch allowance** so the UI moves\n  to the Stake state on real data — never on tx submission.\n\nThis removes the `hasApproved` flag entirely: derive the button from\nconnection state → chain → balance → allowance, and the widget can never show\nan action that cannot work.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5898,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5898},"output_tokens":9,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6a04dca5-bd17-4ddd-ac69-a817e32c8369","uuid":"d2325daf-3813-4f75-bdfe-609226a0c85c","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:31:04.734Z","request_id":"req_011CdLVQSsQFs9PMANG2FLfi"}
